transcript: Why is the 600-ton steel ball hanging from the ceiling in Taipei 101, Taiwan's tallest building? It's because Taiwan sits right on the ring of fire, home of 90% of the world's earthquakes. When you build one of the tallest buildings on earth here, shaking isn't a rare emergency, it's a weekly occurrence. Which is why the solution wasn't to fight the movement, it was to work with it. Because normally if you were to add a fixed weight to the top of something, you would just increase its instability, making it way more top-heavy. However, this weight isn't fixed. it's suspended allowing essentially 100 elephants to swing freely perfectly counteracting the natural sway of the building to keep it in place in hurricanes and earthquakes
metadata_caption: How To Keep a Skyscraper From Falling Over
